body.statement: For every fixed pair of positive constants \(c_0,C_0\), there is \(c_1(c_0,C_0)>0\) such that, whenever \(d\geq2\), \(n\geq c_0d/\log(ed)\), and \(\log(en)\leq C_0\log(ed)\), the minimax mean-squared error for estimating \(\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1\) from two independent samples of respective sizes \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\), one from each of \(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q\in\Delta_d\), is at least \(c_1(c_0,C_0)\min\{1,d/[n\log(en)]\}\).

source.locator: Theorem 3, equation (24), and its Poissonized lower-bound proof
source.verbatim_statement: n≥c S/ln S, ln n≤C ln S ⇒ sup_Q inf_L sup_P E_P|L-||P-Q||_1|² ≳_{c,C} S/(n ln n). The lower bound for the known Q case also serves as a lower bound for the unknown Q case.

attestation.note: Verified 2026-09-07 from primary arXiv:1705.00807v7 TeX, Theorem 3 lower-bound lines 457--465: for every fixed positive c,C the hidden lower constant may depend on c,C; the paper globally works in the Poisson model, and the known-Q lower bound transfers to the unknown-Q experiment. The run separately performs the 2n rescaling and fixed-sample transfer.
